answers.answer: No. SCOPe (current release 2.08, frozen 2021-07-28) does not treat these three groups as one homologous superfamily. It places all three in the same fold, f.21 "Heme-binding four-helical bundle" (sunid 81344, class f: membrane and cell surface proteins), whose fold-level comment describes only a shared architecture: "core: four transmembrane helices, up-and-down bundle, binds one or two heme groups in between the helices". Within that fold they are three distinct superfamilies: f.21.1 "Transmembrane di-heme cytochromes" (sunid 81342; families f.21.1.1 formate dehydrogenase N gamma/cytochrome subunit, f.21.1.2 cytochrome b of the bc1 complex and cytochrome b6, plus f.21.1.0 automated matches), f.21.2 "Fumarate reductase respiratory complex transmembrane subunits" (sunid 81343; families f.21.2.1 FrdC single-chain subunit and f.21.2.2 SdhC/FrdC + SdhD/FrdD two-chain subunits), and f.21.3 "Respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain" (sunid 103501; single family f.21.3.1, Pfam PF02665, E. coli NarI e.g. d1siwc_). In SCOP/SCOPe semantics, sharing a fold means similar topology/architecture that may arise from convergence or physical constraints of packing hemes between transmembrane helices; only the superfamily level asserts probable common ancestry, and only the family level asserts clear homology (sequence or very close structure/function). Homology is therefore asserted within each superfamily (e.g. between bc1 cytochrome b and FdnI in f.21.1, where the curators note three of four heme ligands are conserved; or between FrdC and SdhC/SdhD in f.21.2, where the same fold is built from one chain or two chains), but is explicitly not asserted across f.21.1, f.21.2 and f.21.3. The curators flag the uncertainty themselves: the f.21.3 comment calls NarI a "possible link between the two other superfamilies", being functionally related to the FdnN gamma subunit (f.21.1) yet structurally closer to FrdC (f.21.2). That is a hypothesis recorded as a comment, not a merger, and SCOPe keeps the three superfamilies separate. Practical limits: do not transfer function, heme-ligand positions, quinone-site residues or ancestry claims across these superfamilies on the basis of SCOPe alone; treat cross-superfamily templates as fold-level analogues (useful for topology, unreliable for residue-level modelling). Supporting a single-superfamily claim would need external evidence beyond SCOPe, e.g. statistically significant remote-sequence/profile-HMM relationships (Pfam/ECOD/HHpred-type evidence), conserved heme-ligating histidine positions and helix register across all three groups, or a curated reclassification in a later SCOPe release. Note also that SCOPe's f.21.1.0 automated-matches family only adds members with clear sequence similarity to existing f.21.1 members and does not bridge superfamilies.
